boundary_note: Bounded campaign first pass. No tactical or campaign replacement boundary or canonical opening population has been established. Unresolved phase labels preserve this limit; all claims remain draft prose and supply no model features.

claims.value: The current NPS table displays zero troops on both sides; this is an unresolved source-data problem, not a measured force count.
claims.rationale: The populated narrative contradicts a literal zero. Preserve the snapshot and missingness; do not import the zeros.

claims.value: Grant recalls proposing to take 17,000 men up the Tennessee, with transport capacity insufficient to move them together.
claims.rationale: This is an intended expedition population, not an observed count present at first fire. No opening-strength feature is inferred.

claims.value: Grant estimates about 2,800 in the fort and camp, distinguishes reinforcements halted outside, and later describes about one hundred men left to serve the fort guns.
claims.rationale: These are different populations and phases, not a range or competing counts of a single opening garrison. Grant is a retrospective opposing commander; Tilghman’s report mentioned in context has not been inspected.

claims.value: Grant describes returning transports for Smith’s division and an army approach delayed by absent roads, dense forest and high water.
claims.rationale: The account distinguishes transport concentration from the later approach; neither delay is assigned a numerical effect or a reviewed inherited/created classification.

claims.value: Grant says he used the Essex to test the fort’s gun range while considering a landing above a creek; he describes debarking below it after longer-range fire.
claims.rationale: A retrospective description of his own information gathering and decision, not independent proof of the full contemporary information set.

claims.value: Grant describes possession of Fort Henry as opening navigation up the Tennessee to Muscle Shoals.
claims.rationale: This is retrospective strategic rationale, not an inspected pre-operation directive or a separate campaign success to add to the battle result.

citations.locator: Chapter XXI, local extraction row 392; paragraph begins: The enemy at this time occupied a line running from the Mississippi River at Columbus
citations.quote: With Fort Henry in our hands we had a navigable stream open to us up to Muscle Shoals, in Alabama.

claims.value: Grant describes a plan for troops to invest the garrison while gunboats attacked; NPS records Tilghman surrendering to the fleet after sending most of his force toward Donelson.
claims.rationale: The evidence requires distinct army, naval and Confederate decisions. It does not support assigning the entire outcome to a listed commander.

citations.locator: Chapter XXI, local extraction row 400; paragraph begins: The plan was for the troops and gunboats to start at the same moment. The troops were
citations.quote: The troops were to invest the garrison and the gunboats to attack the fort at close quarters.
While leaving artillery in the fort to hold off the Union fleet, he escorted the rest of his force out of the area and sent them safely off on the route to Fort Donelson, 10 miles away.
Tilghman then returned to the fort and, soon afterwards, surrendered to the fleet

claims.value: The frozen CWSAC result and current NPS summary both label this a Union victory.
claims.rationale: The two records share one source family. This preserves the source classification without assigning commander credit or numerical campaign utility.
